intervals.label: NaI modules deployed at the Kamioka underground laboratory (first configuration)
intervals.note: Per the 2026 review, nine of the 20 NaI modules of ELEGANT V were assembled in 1992 and deployed at Kamioka; the central 36.5 kg detector was used for the dark matter search and the others as active shielding. The sources do not say when this configuration ended.
intervals.quote: 9 were assembled in 1992 and deployed at Kamioka Underground Laboratory.

intervals.note: The 2006 PICO-LON paper speaks of the old lead 'which was used for the shield of ELEGANT V' (past tense). The latest source that shows ELEGANT V running is the 2001 annual report; its Oto limits are shown in a 2005 paper (arXiv:astro-ph/0506329). No shutdown date is published.

summary.plain: ELEGANT V was a 0.76-ton array of sodium iodide crystals in Japan's Oto Cosmo Observatory, an underground laboratory in Nara, used to search for dark matter alongside double-beta-decay studies. Its crystals and lead shield later served the PICO-LON dark matter project.
summary.technical: ELEGANT V (ELEctron GAmma-ray Neutrino Telescope V) at the Oto Cosmo Observatory: 16 NaI(Tl) scintillators (0.76 tons) inside lead and copper shields with drift chambers and plastic scintillators around a 100Mo double-beta source; the NaI array was used for dark matter searches (spin-dependent limits and an annual modulation search per the 2002 overview). An earlier configuration with nine NaI modules (central 36.5 kg detector) was deployed at Kamioka in 1992 (threshold 4 keV, background ~5.1 cpd/kg/keV at 5 keV).
